title: Fresh seed 5 (own mutation draws), T=10000: the waste vortices again exceed the kind-blind twin in classes reached (71 vs 44 reaching activity 5; 39 vs 22 held by >=3), diversity (1.0 vs 0.5) and replacement (17% vs 31% of 1000-t-old classes still present), but not in first-time dominants (3 vs 5 after t=3000) or in c30's significant new kinds (2 vs 1 late); split parents sit where similar vortices are locally scarce in both arms alike, so local rarity is not what the waste adds
summary: c58's trait3d world (ew 0.25, sw 0.4, mut_dt 50) and its kind-blind twin (sw 0, same draws) on seed 5 with mut_seed 5, run with trait3c.py (trait3.py plus checkpoint/resume every 250 t; a resumed run reproduces an uninterrupted one exactly). Waste arm: classes held by >=3 vortices 12/20/22/39 at t=1500/3000/4500/10000 (twin 6/12/16/22); reaching activity 5: 71 vs 44, per 1000 t 9,17,8,5,5,6,7,9,1,4 vs 10,5,8,3,3,3,1,9,0,2; first-time dominants after t=3000 3 vs 5; distinct dominants 8 vs 6; c30 cohort novelty (a* = twin max 64): 5,3,0,1,0,0,1,0,0,0 vs 2,0,0,1,0,0,0,0,0,0 (late 2 vs 1); top-5 overlap with the first window 0-0.4 vs 0.2-0.6; diversity 1.04 vs 0.49; centroid MSD at lag 1000 t 0.079 vs 0.016; class survival over 1000 t 0.17 vs 0.31. Heredity: 119 trait jumps at mutations, 1 elsewhere (twin 156/0); 131/152 daughters keep the class (twin 402/460). Local rarity (rarity.py, R=22 px, the waste's reach; similarity kernel width 0.4): split parents have fewer similar neighbours than the average vortex in both arms (difference -0.23, p=0.05 in the waste arm; -0.43, p<0.001 in the twin), so being locally rare at division is generic crowding, not the waste's kind-specific effect.

finding.operator: kind-specific waste on a 3-component heritable trait
finding.control: kind-blind waste twin (sw 0, same draws), fresh seed 5 / mut_seed 5, T=10000; local-rarity test against the same twin
finding.result: classes reaching activity 5: 71 vs 44; first-time dominants after t=3000: 3 vs 5; c30 significant new kinds late: 2 vs 1; split parents' local similarity minus mean: -0.23 (waste) vs -0.43 (twin)

limits: Across the five seeds (c58's 1-3 and c59's 4-5), the waste arm always reaches more classes, keeps more diversity and moves its trait centroid faster. The stricter measures are mixed. First-time dominants after t=3000 are 10/9/3 against 1/2/5 on the T=10000 seeds. c30's significant new kinds after t~3300 are 2/1/4/7/2 against 1/0/1/0/1. On seeds 3-5 that rate falls to about 0.4 per 1000 t after t~5000. So the evidence does not yet meet L8's 'does not saturate', and I did not write a C:open-ended claim. The 'ends' in rarity.py include merges and short segmentation gaps (2800+ per run), so the death side of the rarity test is weak. One parameter point, 128^2, no dt/2, grid or box-size test.
